text:
maria.yang: Heads-up: nightly GPU smoke red on kv-cache tests for the multi-tenant shard (only on h100-pool-3). Seeing corrupted kv entries + OOMs. Link to shard logs: https://ci.internal/runs/1758001122/log
kenji: ack. can you paste the failing log snippet? is this reproducing locally or only in CI?
maria.yang: only CI so far. snippet from worker-7:
```
[2026-02-12T01:12:33Z] ERROR model_serving: kv cache miss -> returning corrupted token (len mismatch)
[2026-02-12T01:12:33Z] WARN gpu_mgr: attempted alloc 234MB -> OOM (allocated 114GB / 128GB)
[2026-02-12T01:12:33Z] TRACE kv_cache: checksum mismatch, expected 0x3f2a got 0x0
```
kenji: hmm checksum mismatch suggests either a write concurrency bug or KV memory aliasing across tenants. ashley any recent KV allocator changes merged?
ashley: I touched the kv-cache LRU eviction last week (PR #4321) but it was just a heuristic tweak, not memory layout. however david reverted a patch on allocator last month that we reintroduced in a followup.
david: I suspect allocator+continuous batching interaction. quick bisect candidate: try between commits a1f3c4 -> b2d9e7 (allocator change). run `git bisect` on the bisection range with the smoke test.
kenji: before bisect, can you try a single-tenant run on the same node image? if it passes, likely multi-tenant interference.
maria.yang: ok kicking a single-tenant job on h100-pool-3 with the same test config now. @ci-bot can you enqueue a rerun of the flaky shard but with 1 concurrency? ci-bot: rerun queued: build/1758001122 -> build/1758001123 :eyes:
nisha: also try reproducing with older driver image (nv-driver:535.86) — we recently bumped to 536.x in the canary. driver mismatches have caused weird alloc behavior before.
kenji: good call. also check dmesg for Xid errors. `sudo dmesg | tail -n 50` on the worker shows if kernel-side GPU faults happened.
maria.yang: pasted dmesg from worker-7 earlier:
```
[ 1234.567890] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 31, PID=4321, Threaded-ptx-jit
[ 1234.568000] NVRM: GPU at 0000:65:00: GPU has fallen off the bus.
```
maria.yang: single-tenant run started, will report in ~6m.
ashley: if single-tenant passes, next step is reproducer that stashes KV then runs another tenant to see if corruption surfaces. small repro command:
```
# run repro on node
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 python -u tests/repro_kv_corrupt.py --iters 100 --worker-threads 2
```
kenji: thanks. if you can capture `strace -f` and `nvprof` for the failing process that'd be gold.
ci-bot: rerun started: build/1758001123
maria.yang: single-tenant passed, no corruption. multi-tenant rerun still queued.
david: then likely cross-tenant memory reuse; try setting `RDW_KV_ISOLATION=1` env on the runner as a quick guard. can we add a canary job with that flag?
nisha: I can spin a canary image with older driver too, running now.
maria.yang: canary started: build/1758001124 (nv-driver:535.86) — will compare outputs.
kenji: awesome. if canary passes and multi-tenant with flag passes, we have a mitigation path: ship RDW_KV_ISOLATION default and schedule allocator fix.
ashley: filing a quick issue: https://issues.internal/RED-9287 (kvcache cross-tenant corruption investigation)
maria.yang: noted. tagging owners: @kenji @david @nisha. I'll paste follow-up logs once reruns complete. :thumbsup:
ci-bot: build/1758001123 finished: red -> failing tests unchanged
ci-bot: build/1758001124 finished: green (canary with older driver)
maria.yang: ok canary green on 535.86; multi-tenant still failing on 536.x. looks like driver bump likely exposed a race.
kenji: thanks. next: nudge infra to hold 536.x rollout, and schedule bisect on allocator commits. I'll open a quick PR to set RDW_KV_ISOLATION=1 as an opt-in Canary.
david: running bisect now, will update thread with commit that regresses.
maria.yang: appreciated — closing loop once we have repro/bisect. thanks everyone. :raised_hands:
